newsitem.title: UK: British watchdog says EU gas directive "flawed".
newsitem.headline: British watchdog says EU gas directive "flawed".

text.p: Britain's gas industry regulator said on Tuesday proposals for a European Union gas directive were flawed because they did require monopolies to separate supply activities from transport operations.
"This is something fundamentally flawed in the European gas directive," regulator Clare Spottiswoode told a conference.
Spottiswoode said a split between the two businesses was essential to make the introduction of competition in gas markets work.

Britain is leading Europe in opening up gas markets. The market for big users here was liberalised in the early 1990s, while the domestic supply market is on schedule for nationwide competition in 1998, Spottiswoode said.
The UK government in 1993 demanded that former monopoly British Gas separate its supply activities from its pipeline operations, where competition cannot be introduced in practice.
British Gas first erected a Chinese wall and an actual demerger of the transport activities is scheduled to take place next month.

The separation ensured that newcomers in the market felt there was a level playing field without the pipeline business cross-subsidising British Gas' supply activities, Spottiswoode told a conference on competition policy.
